messages:
Sanjay: FYI I'm seeing rapid promote/demote churn for a handful of prefixes during tenant surges. hit-rate spikes for ~30s and then vanishes — we demote, then immediately promote again. Causing IO thrash and higher tail latency.
Maya: Ugh. Is this the same tenant that hit the hotset rollercoaster last week? :grimacing:
Sanjay: Yep, same pattern. It looks like our promotion decision is purely short-window EWMA without hysteresis.
Lee: Can you paste the metric slices? rough numbers help.
Sanjay: Sure — peek at the prefix pfx_42: hit_rate 0.85 -> 0.12 within 45s, evict_score toggles between 0.9 and 0.2; promotion_count 6 in 2m.
Oz: Sounds like we need a promotion hysteresis + demotion delay. Also consider coupling with global admission/backpressure so we don't aggressively pin when the node is overloaded.
Anita: Agree. For demotion we currently use a single threshold crossing. We should require either sustained low hit-rate for X windows OR explicit eviction_credit pressure.
Maya: Proposal: add two knobs — promo_streak and demote_cooldown. Promo requires N consecutive windows above threshold; demote waits M seconds after promotion before eligible.
CI-Bot: PR opened: https://git.internal/rdw/pr/2129 — implements promo_streak and demote_cooldown with defaults (N=3, M=60). CI: tests pending.
Infra: We need telemetry to show time-since-last-promotion, promotion_attempts, and demote_eligible boolean per-prefix. Otherwise ops can't debug.
Lee: Also add a token bucket for promotions per-shard so a noisy tenant can't starve out others by constantly consuming promotion slots.
Sanjay: Good call. We also need to avoid a pathological case: a prefix flapping just around threshold still consuming promotion quota. We should add exponential backoff multiplier on consecutive promotions.
Anita: Example config sketch I threw together:
```
promote_threshold: 0.6
promo_streak: 3        # windows
demote_threshold: 0.25
demote_cooldown: 60    # seconds after promote before eligible
promo_backoff: [1, 2, 4]  # multiplier on cooldown after repeated promotes
promo_quota_per_shard: 5
```
Lee: Love it. Need to ensure these defaults don't break low-throughput tenants (tiny prefixes) — maybe scale thresholds by prefix request volume.
Oz: Also think about atomicity: promotion decision is local but eviction/placement is cluster-aware. If we promote locally but handoff moves prefix, we need idempotent promotion attempts. Add idempotent promotion RPC with lease check.
Maya: That's new: an invariant where promotion token must be valid for min_hold window. If handoff occurs, the new owner inherits the token TTL. Avoids double promotions.
Sanjay: Can someone capture this as a follow-up RFC item? This impacts handoff + promotion interplay.
Anita: I'll add a section in the existing prefix-cache RFC (see 'promotion semantics' subsection) describing: streak-based promos, demote cooldown, per-shard quota, backoff, telemetry fields, and idempotent promotion RPC.
CI-Bot: Draft PR created: https://git.internal/rdw/pr/2130 — docs + tests skeleton.
Infra: I'll add tracing spans for promotion_attempt -> promotion_commit -> demote_eligibility. Also add an alert when promotion_rate_per_shard > promo_quota * 2 for 5m.
Lee: Ops question: on rollout, can we put defaults conservative (N=5, M=120) and then iterate? Safer for customers.
Maya: Agreed; start conservative. We'll stress test on canary nodes with a scripted churning tenant.
Sanjay: I'll put together a small chaos test that simulates sinusoidal request spikes to validate oscillation elimination.
Oz: One more thing — make sure batching/prefetch doesn't break streak calculations (e.g., a batched burst looks like one big window). We should compute hit-rate normalized by effective windows, not raw aggregated bursts.
Anita: Noted — will call that out in tests.
Maya: Nice progress. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Lee: SGTM — I'll review the PRs this afternoon.
Sanjay: Thanks — ping me on thread for reviews or if QA finds regressions.
